twenty_m.rule: Page default need: 240 sunlit hours and 100 hours of Earth contact (illustrative) in 14 days, Earth only with a NASA ground station 10 degrees up, 13 touchdown points within 100 m, 60 landing dates. A point agrees when both grids give the same answer to 'do all 13 touchdown points pass on the planned date'.

ridge.published_note: Published longest darkness at this point, as cited in the entry's validation notes (not recomputed: it is the literature value we check against).

regions.rule: A region is open at a landing time when at least one of its published candidate sites (Wueller et al. 2026) is a clear Yes that is not fragile: a 6.25-day stay with the Sun up every hour, checked at 13 touchdown points within 100 m. 'Earth need' adds 100 hours of Earth contact with a NASA ground station; the 100 hours are illustrative, not a NASA requirement. Best sets are found by trying every combination. Shares are of landing times every 6 hours, not of launch opportunities.

season_drift.expected_note: 365.25 days minus the eclipse year (346.62 days): the Moon's tilted orbit turns once in 18.6 years, so the polar summer comes back about 18.6 days earlier each calendar year.
season_drift.how: Slipday's own ephemeris, daily: the day each year when the Sun stands furthest south of the lunar equator, then a straight-line fit (2025 to 2035, and 2025 to 2032 like the region calendar); and a sine wave fitted to the daily sub-solar latitude, whose best period is the season cycle.
